The Agentic AI Risk Gap: From Autonomy to Accountability
description:
[Register here to receive your access link!](https://ctrly.io/Jhhfv )

AI agents are moving beyond answering questions to writing code, accessing enterprise data, connecting to business tools, and executing workflows autonomously. While these capabilities can unlock significant productivity gains, they also introduce new security, governance, and accountability challenges.

**How can teams give AI agents the freedom to work effectively while ensuring they operate within the right boundaries?** From managing permissions and mitigating prompt injection risks to establishing human oversight, building trust in autonomous systems requires the right safeguards.

Join technology, AI, and security leaders for a practical discussion on deploying and scaling agentic AI responsibly. We'll explore emerging risks, proven safeguards, and strategies for balancing innovation with security and accountability.

**What You'll Learn**

* Emerging risks in agentic AI, including prompt injection, unintended actions, and data access concerns.
* Establishing permissions, guardrails, and human oversight for autonomous systems.
* Security best practices, including least-privilege access, monitoring, and auditability.
* Strategies for scaling agentic AI while balancing innovation, governance, and accountability.

name: AI Alignment and Control: Risks as AI Surpasses Human Abilities
description:
**A free, 90-minute online workshop—no technical background needed**
AI is no longer just getting better at narrow tasks. Today's systems can write, code, reason through problems, and increasingly take actions on their own, and AI is starting to move into the physical world through robotics. Many researchers believe we are heading toward AI that matches or exceeds human abilities across a wide range of areas.
That raises two of the most important questions in AI today. Can we make sure these systems actually do what we intend (**alignment**)? And can we keep the ability to oversee, correct, or stop them as they become more capable (**control**)?
This workshop explains these ideas in plain English, without hype or jargon, and looks at what they could mean for your job, your relationships, and your day-to-day life.
Together, we'll explore questions like:

* **Smarter-than-human AI:** What would it mean for AI to outperform people across most tasks, and how is that different from today's AI tools?
* **Alignment:** Why is it so hard to make sure an AI system pursues the goals we actually want, and what happens when it doesn't?
* **Control:** How do researchers try to monitor and correct AI systems, and why might that get harder as AI becomes more capable?
* **Work and daily life:** Which jobs are already being automated or transformed, and how is AI starting to fill roles once held by coworkers, tutors, therapists, and companions?

**What you'll get:**

* A clear, beginner-friendly introduction to AI alignment and control, and why they matter
* Real-world examples of how AI is already reshaping work and social life
* Live demos that highlight both impressive capabilities and emerging risks
* Interactive discussion and exercises to test your own intuitions about the future

Come ready to grapple with one of the biggest transitions humanity may ever face, a shift that could redefine how we work, how we relate to each other, and who stays in control.

* Creating reusable coding harnesses
* Managing context across large repositories
* Running tests and validating agent-generated changes
* Using sandboxes, permissions, and approval steps
* Coordinating subagents or parallel tasks

* Debugging failed or incomplete agent runs

You do not need to be an expert in either tool. This meetup is for people who want hands-on time to experiment, pair with other developers, and learn through building.

name: (CS)²AI Online: Cyber-Informed Engineering (CIE):  Bridging the OT Divide
description:
**Control systems are under constant threat, and patching and monitoring alone can’t stop an attacker who is determined and well resourced. Cyber-Informed Engineering (CIE) takes a different approach. It builds security into how systems are designed and operated, so the worst consequences can be engineered out.**

**Join Virginia “Ginger” Wright, CIE Program Manager at Idaho National Laboratory, for a session on what CIE looks like in practice. Ginger leads INL’s work on the DOE National Strategy for CIE and wrote the CIE Implementation Guide. She has also testified before the U.S. Senate on the subject.**
**You’ll leave with:**

* **A clear grounding in CIE. The session starts with a quick primer, so no background is needed.**
* **A current view of the threats to control systems. You’ll see what adversaries are doing now and why traditional defenses fall short.**
* **A real-world case study. It shows how CIE thinking changes outcomes.**
* **Hands-on knowledge of the tools for applying CIE. The main focus is how to use them, including the Engineering Controls Database.**

**Who should attend: ICS/OT security practitioners, control systems and process engineers, IT/OT convergence teams, asset owners and operators, security leaders, and anyone building a career in critical infrastructure protection.**

***Whether you’re an engineer learning security or a security professional learning engineering, this session gives you methods you can use right away.***

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

name: Databricks CustomerLake
description:
**Marketing teams are investing heavily in AI, but many still struggle to connect that spend to clear business results.**

**Join** PhillyBricks, the Databricks User Group for Greater Philadelphia, for an evening on Databricks CustomerLake. This is the final PhillyBricks meetup of 2026, so you don’t want to miss it!

Marketing is shifting from an attention economy to a prediction economy. It controls the largest discretionary AI budget in the enterprise, with an estimated $463B in productivity opportunity, yet only 3% of CMOs can prove even half of it (McKinsey, State of Marketing 2026). CustomerLake (and Decision Intelligence) close that gap. This session looks at how Databricks CustomerLake approaches the problem.

Jayesh Patel, Strategic Growth at Lumenalta, and Dilorom Abdullah, Databricks Practice Director at Lumenalta, Databricks MVP & Partner Champion, will explain how CustomerLake and Decision Intelligence work on the Databricks platform followed by a demo. We’ll open with networking, food and drinks, then dive into the technical talk before wrapping up.

A huge thank you to our Gold Sponsor, Lumenalta, for backing this event, and to Microsoft for hosting us at their Malvern office.
Whether you’re deep into Databricks or just getting started, come connect with fellow data practitioners from across the region. Free to attend, registration required. [https://usergroups.databricks.com/e/m9shce/]

\*All guests must be on the attendee list for entry:
https://usergroups.databricks.com/e/m9shce/
